headline.en: A round is a canon that loops back to the start. A canon can begin at any distance or pitch: here, a bar behind and an octave away.

headline.en: Songs on the same chords, in the same time, often fit together. Singing two at once is a quodlibet, Latin for "whatever you please".

headline.en: Some notes sound smooth together, some rub. In this style unisons, thirds, fifths, sixths and octaves are smooth; seconds, fourths and sevenths rub, and a rub wants to move.

detail.en: Do to mi: skip one note

title.en: A fifth, a sixth, an octave

detail.en: Do to so, to la, to do
Re over do, or fa: it leans, then steps home

text.en: Over the drone: smooth or rubbing?

why.en: Mi over do, a third: smooth.
Re over do, a ninth: it rubs and wants to step down.
So over do, a fifth: smooth and open.
Ti over do, a seventh: it rubs and wants to rise to do.
La over do, a sixth: smooth.
Fa over do, a fourth: in this style it rubs, and steps down to mi.

text.en: In 1863 Hermann von Helmholtz explained a rub as beating: overtones close in pitch wobbling against each other.

headline.en: Two voices can move the same way, opposite ways, or one can hold while the other moves. Opposite ways keeps them most independent.

detail.en: The same way (parallel, if the distance stays)
Opposite ways

prompt.en: How did the two voices move?

why.en: Both climbed together: similar motion. When they keep the same distance, it's parallel.

prompt.en: How did the two voices move?

why.en: One climbed while the other fell: contrary motion, the surest way to sound like two voices.

prompt.en: How did the two voices move?

why.en: The top held while the bottom climbed: oblique motion.

prompt.en: How did the two voices move?

why.en: Up against down again: contrary motion.
A moves in fifths: the two voices fuse into one hollow sound, B's thirds keep them two.
B moves in fifths and sounds bare. A moves in sixths, sweet and full. That's why counterpoint avoids parallel fifths.

headline.en: In 1725 Johann Joseph Fux taught counterpoint in steps he called species. The first is note against note: one of your notes to each note of a cantus, a slow, fixed tune.

text.en: Fux wrote his book as a dialogue: the teacher, Aloysius, stands for Palestrina, and the student, Josephus, for Fux himself.

headline.en: Hold a note into the next chord, where it rubs, then fall a step: a suspension, one of the oldest ways to make a listener lean in.

detail.en: While the bass moves under you

why.en: B holds do over the new chord, where it rubs, then lets go. A steps down as the chord changes: smooth, but no lean.

prompt.en: Which one leans before it lands?

why.en: B leans: the held do rubs over the new chord, then lands on ti. A steps down as the chord changes: smooth, but no lean. Composers have loved that lean for centuries.
